A_target.statement:
Let $\sim$ identify $0$ and $1$ in $\closedint 0 1$.
Then $\closedint 0 1 / \sim$ is [[Definition:Homeomorphic|homeomorphic]] to the circle $\Bbb S^1$.

B_source.statement:
Let $q: X \to X / \sim$ be a [[Definition:Quotient Mapping|quotient mapping]].
Then continuous mappings $X / \sim \to Y$ correspond to continuous mappings $X \to Y$ which are constant on equivalence classes.

object_map.reformulation: Find a continuous surjection whose fibres are exactly the equivalence classes, and let it descend.

validity_conditions: The fibres of the exponential map on [0, 1] are exactly the classes of the relation.
A continuous bijection from a compact space to a Hausdorff space is a homeomorphism.
proof_plan: Let $\map e t = e^{2 \pi i t}$, a continuous surjection $\closedint 0 1 \to \Bbb S^1$.
$\map e s = \map e t$ {{iff}} $s = t$ or $\set {s, t} = \set {0, 1}$, so the fibres of $e$ are exactly the classes of $\sim$.
By the source result, $e$ induces a continuous [[Definition:Bijection|bijection]] $\bar e: \closedint 0 1 / \sim \to \Bbb S^1$.
